goal: Make Docket's prompt and schedule editing feel less clunky: text fields that grow and read as markdown, and a weekly grid for posting slots.

entries.title: 1. Auto-growing, monospace prompt and instruction fields
entries.description:
Entry 1 of 2 in the UI tweaks roadmap: readable prompt and instruction text fields. This entry is the shared-primitive and typography work; entry 2 (week-slot-grid) builds the weekly posting-slot grid and must inherit the type scale this entry settles, which is why this one goes first.

The reported problem, in the user's words: "We're doing a lot of textareas to describe instructions or prompts. Since prompts can be in markdown we should at least display that as monospace font. I think all of the copy could stand to be smaller text as well. I'm looking at spots like under 'voice' and it seems like we should do text fields that grow with the copy so you don't have to do internal scrolling."

Three things to fix, in order of importance:

1. A shared auto-growing textarea primitive. There is no `Textarea` in src/components/ui/ today — all 13 textareas are hand-rolled `<textarea>` elements with `controlStyles` and a `rows` guess, and src/app/p/[projectSlug]/voice/VoiceEditor.tsx has grown its own private labelled-textarea wrapper (around line 55-80) that other screens then copied. Add `TextareaField` to src/components/ui/ alongside Field.tsx, matching Field's contract exactly: `id` required, `label`, `hint` and `error` wired through `aria-describedby`, error in an `aria-live="polite"` region, `aria-invalid` from `error`, `controlStyles` for the chrome. It must grow with its content instead of scrolling internally: a `minRows` floor and an optional `maxRows` ceiling after which it does scroll, so a 400-line prompt cannot push the submit button off screen. Prefer CSS `field-sizing: content` with a scripted fallback (set `height` from `scrollHeight` on input and on mount) so it also grows for server-rendered initial values and for programmatic value changes, not only while typing. Keep it usable as a controlled and an uncontrolled component, and make sure it works in a `<Dialog>` where the initial measure happens while the element may still be hidden.

2. Monospace for markdown. Add a `mono` option to the primitive (`font-mono`, per the existing "Code, slugs, keys" row in the docs/design-system.md type scale) and turn it on for the fields that hold prompts, instructions or other markdown, not for fields that hold post copy or short prose. Starting classification, to be checked against each field's actual label and purpose before changing it: monospace for src/app/p/[projectSlug]/accounts/PostingInstructionsForm.tsx:54, src/app/p/[projectSlug]/generate/GenerateForm.tsx:71, src/app/p/[projectSlug]/generate/result/[postId]/RegenerateDialog.tsx:42, src/app/p/[projectSlug]/generate/SeriesPlanEditor.tsx:74, src/app/p/[projectSlug]/jobs/new/JobForm.tsx:169 and src/app/p/[projectSlug]/voice/VoiceEditor.tsx:68; proportional for the two in src/app/p/[projectSlug]/compose/Composer.tsx:366 and :413, src/app/p/[projectSlug]/generate/result/[postId]/VariantEditor.tsx:110, src/app/p/[projectSlug]/media/MediaEditDialog.tsx:39, src/app/p/[projectSlug]/review/RejectDialog.tsx:45, src/app/p/[projectSlug]/voice/TryItPanel.tsx:102 and src/components/media/MediaPicker.tsx:41. Where a field renders a counter or a limit against a character budget, check the monospace change does not break its alignment.

3. Smaller supporting copy. The user's "all of the copy could stand to be smaller" is about explanatory and helper text crowding the forms, not about shrinking everything. docs/design-system.md section 4 already defines the scale (14 px `text-sm` body, 12 px `text-xs` caption/hint). Apply it consistently on the form-heavy screens rather than inventing a new scale: descriptions, hints and helper paragraphs that currently render at `text-sm` inside a form should drop to `text-xs text-muted-foreground`, while labels, control text and anything a person types stay at `text-sm` — never shrink the text inside a control, and never go below 12 px. The "under voice" spot the user named is the one to get right first: read src/app/p/[projectSlug]/voice/ in full and make that screen the reference. Do not change the PageHeader description convention or table typography.

Adopt the primitive at all 13 sites listed above, delete VoiceEditor's private wrapper, and add the `TextareaField` row to the primitives table in docs/design-system.md (section around line 240, next to the `controlStyles` row) with a line in section 4 recording when monospace applies. Follow docs/design-system.md and the docket-ui skill. Keep every form a server action away from working as it does now: this entry changes presentation and one shared component, not a single server action, validation schema or service.

Testing: a component test for `TextareaField` covering label/hint/error wiring and `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` from `error`, the `minRows` floor, growth past it, and the `maxRows` ceiling turning scrolling back on; a test that the mono option emits `font-mono` and that a non-mono field does not; a test that an initial server-rendered value is measured on mount, not only on first keystroke. src/app/p/[projectSlug]/voice/voice.test.tsx:160 asserts `<textarea[^>]*aria-describedby="..."` against rendered markup — keep that assertion passing, and update it only if the attribute order genuinely changes. Run the full suite: these are shared styles and a shared primitive, so breakage will be in screens this entry did not mean to touch.

NOT included, and no later entry in this roadmap owns any of it: a markdown preview pane or split editor; syntax highlighting; a rich-text or CodeMirror/Monaco editor; changing what any prompt field stores or validates; a project-wide font or token change in globals.css; a density or compact-mode preference. Entry 2 owns the posting-slot week grid and all slot behaviour — do not touch src/app/p/[projectSlug]/accounts/SlotEditor.tsx or the slot table on the accounts page beyond the supporting-copy pass, and leave the slots service and its actions alone.
entries.rationale: First because it settles the shared textarea primitive and the type scale; the week grid in entry 2 should be built against the final scale rather than need a follow-up pass. It is also the lower-risk of the two, so it lands while the base is quiet.

entries.title: 2. Reusable week grid for posting slots
entries.description:
Entry 2 of 2 in the UI tweaks roadmap: a reusable weekly posting-slot grid, replacing the per-account day-and-time picker. Entry 1 (prompt-text-fields) has landed; inherit the type scale it settled and use its `TextareaField` if this entry needs a textarea at all.

The reported problem, in the user's words: "Date/time picker for each account feels clunky in its current state. Could we instead do a reusable component of a horizontal row of a week with the ability to place, drag, and edit timeslots in each column of the day? Hovering over each timeslot could reveal an X to delete it. Clicking the date would toggle it active/inactive."

What exists now. src/app/p/[projectSlug]/accounts/page.tsx renders, per account, a `Table` of posting slots with Day / Time / Status / Actions columns (around lines 224-248), one `SlotRowActions` per row (Pause/Resume plus a two-step confirm Delete), and below it `SlotEditor` — a `SegmentedControl` of Mon-Sun plus a `type="time"` `Field` and an "Add slot" button (src/app/p/[projectSlug]/accounts/SlotEditor.tsx:14-47). That add-then-find-the-row-again loop is the clunkiness. A slot is `{ id, socialAccountId, weekday, localTime, paused }` (src/server/services/slots.ts:10); weekday is 1-7 with Monday 1, matching the `DAYS` array in SlotEditor.tsx:11 and the `WEEKDAYS` lookup on the accounts page. Times are shown in the project time zone, which the accounts page already has in scope.

Build a `WeekSlotGrid` in src/components/schedule/ (the directory exists and holds only explicit-time-text.ts today) as a reusable, presentational client component: seven columns Mon-Sun across a horizontal row, each column holding that day's timeslot chips ordered by time. It takes slots plus callbacks and holds no knowledge of accounts or server actions, so a later caller — the calendar, a project-wide slot view — can reuse it. The accounts page is its first and only caller in this entry.

Interactions, all four of which must work by keyboard and by pointer:
- Place: click or tap an empty spot in a day column to add a slot on that day. Rounding the drop position to a sensible granularity (a 15- or 30-minute step) is fine and probably better than a pixel-exact time, but the created time must then be editable.
- Drag: drag a chip within its column to change its time, and across columns to change its day. This needs a server-side move that does not exist yet — add `moveSlot` to src/server/services/slots.ts and a `moveSlotAction` to src/app/p/[projectSlug]/accounts/actions.ts, taking `{ id, weekday, localTime }`, enforcing `slot: ["manage"]` the same way `setSlotPaused` and `deleteSlot` do, inside a `scope.transaction`, with the same duplicate-slot rejection `addSlot` gets from `addSlotSchema` in src/lib/validation/scheduling.ts — reuse that validation rather than writing a second rule. A drag onto an occupied time must be refused visibly and the chip must snap back, not silently collide or silently overwrite.
- Edit: let a slot's time be typed, not only dragged, so a precise time is reachable without pixel aiming. A small inline time input on the chip is enough.
- Delete: an X revealed on hover over a chip, and always present for keyboard focus and for touch, since hover does not exist on touch. Deleting a slot is destructive but cheap and re-addable, so the current two-step confirm can go — say so in the spec rather than leaving it ambiguous.
- Toggle active/inactive: clicking the chip body toggles `paused` via the existing `setSlotPausedAction`. Paused chips read as clearly inactive (muted, not merely a shade different) and the state is in text for a screen reader, not carried by colour alone.

Optimistic updates with a rollback on a rejected action, because every one of these is a round trip to a server action. Respect the existing role rules: `slot: ["manage"]` gates every mutation, and an editor who cannot manage slots sees the grid read-only with no drag handles, no X and no add affordance — never a control they cannot use. Keep the slot count and active/paused summary the accounts page already shows accurate after each change.

Accessibility is the hard part here and must not be an afterthought: drag-and-drop needs a keyboard path (focus a chip, then arrow keys or an explicit move mode to change day and time, Enter to commit, Escape to cancel), every chip needs an accessible name carrying day, time and active/paused state, and each change needs an `aria-live` announcement — the repo already has `src/components/ui/Announce.tsx` and `LiveRegion.tsx`; use them rather than a new mechanism. Honour `prefers-reduced-motion` for any snap or drag animation.

Replace the Day/Time/Status/Actions table and `SlotEditor` on the accounts page with the grid. Delete `SlotEditor`'s add-slot form and `SlotRowActions` once nothing uses them; leave `ReconnectMockButton` and `MockBehaviourForm`, which live in the same file and are unrelated. Keep the "Posting slots" definition copy and the time-zone note. Add the component to docs/design-system.md and to the docket-ui skill's conventions, and check docs/accounts.md for anything describing the old add-slot flow. Follow docs/design-system.md and the docket-ui skill.

Testing: unit tests for `moveSlot` — permission denied for a role without `slot: ["manage"]`, `NotFoundError` for a missing slot, duplicate day-and-time rejected, a successful move across days; component tests for the grid placing, moving, editing, deleting and toggling a slot, for the read-only editor view, for a refused move rolling back, and for the keyboard path through all of place/move/delete/toggle; an integration test that the accounts page renders a week of real slots and that a change persists. Run the full suite — the accounts page is heavily tested and this removes a table other tests may assert against; update those assertions to the grid rather than deleting the tests.

NOT included, and no later entry owns it: a month or day calendar view, or any change to src/app/p/[projectSlug]/calendar/; slots at any granularity other than the current weekly day-plus-time; copying a week of slots between accounts; bulk editing across accounts; time-zone-per-account; anything that reschedules already-queued posts when a slot moves — a moved slot affects future scheduling only, and existing targets keep their times exactly as `deleteSlot` already documents.
entries.rationale: Second because it is the larger change, needs a new moveSlot service and action, and replaces a heavily tested table — it wants a base where the shared form primitives have already settled.
